name: Comparable_CompareToNull
protocol: before call(* java.lang.Comparable+.compareTo(..)) with args(o) ∧ (o == null) → emit CRITICAL diagnostic
important_note: This is a runtime call-site rule, not a source-text rule: it reports only when the argument value bound as o is null at a matched invocation. It does not establish that the source literally wrote null, that compareTo executed successfully, that a NullPointerException was thrown, or that the reported application method contains a security vulnerability.

events.name: nullcompare
events.condition: Observation clause: call(* Comparable+.compareTo(..)) && args(o). Reporting predicate: if(o == null), evaluated at the call join point immediately before the invocation. Comparable resolves to java.lang.Comparable because the rule imports java.lang.*, and Comparable+ denotes Comparable and its subtypes. args(o) binds the runtime argument value as java.lang.Object; satisfying the predicate depends on that runtime value being null, not on lexical use of the token null.

forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: Do not infer that name.gdr.acastus_photon.MainActivity.handleIntent contains the literal source expression compareTo(null); a variable, field read, return value, cast, or other expression may evaluate to null at runtime.
Do not infer that every method named compareTo is governed. The rule is scoped to the AspectJ signature pattern Comparable+.compareTo(..), not arbitrary namesake APIs or Comparator.compare methods.
Do not infer that the receiver's exact concrete class is java.lang.Comparable; Comparable+ includes java.lang.Comparable and its subtypes.
Do not infer that the called compareTo implementation ran to completion or threw NullPointerException; the advice runs before the call.
Do not infer exploitability, attacker control, confidentiality impact, integrity impact, availability impact, or any security vulnerability from this diagnostic alone.
Do not infer the exact text or origin of __DEFAULT_MESSAGE from this rule file; the rule explicitly supplies only the additional literal message "null cannot be compared to any object".
semantic_scope: The rule observes woven AspectJ method-call join points whose matched method signature is named compareTo and whose declaring-type pattern is java.lang.Comparable or a subtype. It binds the argument as Object and emits a critical log before the invocation only if the bound runtime reference is null. The representative finding's class and method identify a reported application location, but they do not change the governed API from java.lang.Comparable.compareTo.

detector_semantics.claim: A null argument was supplied at runtime to a call join point selected by call(* Comparable+.compareTo(..)) && args(o), so the monitor emitted a CRITICAL diagnostic before invocation.
predicates: args(o), where the advice parameter is java.lang.Object
limitations: The rule has one event and no state machine or cross-event ordering requirement beyond the before advice timing.
The rule neither observes nor validates the return value, exception, comparison ordering, receiver state, or implementation of compareTo.

A source-level search for compareTo( is only a triage aid: it can miss formatting variations, generated/compiled code, inherited or bridge dispatch, and Kotlin operator syntax that may compile to a compareTo invocation.
The rule's signature pattern is not equivalent to matching every object that happens to be Comparable at runtime; it is a method-call signature pattern using Comparable+.

documented_behavior: java.lang.Comparable<T> defines int compareTo(T o) to compare the receiver with a specified object for order, returning a negative integer, zero, or a positive integer.
Oracle's current Java API documentation states that compareTo throws NullPointerException if the specified object is null.
The Java SE 6 documentation linked by the rule states that e.compareTo(null) should throw NullPointerException because null is not an instance of any class.
preconditions: The receiver participates in the java.lang.Comparable natural-ordering contract.
The comparison argument should be non-null.
The argument must be of a type that can be compared with the receiver; otherwise the API permits ClassCastException.
unknowns: The rule does not identify the concrete Comparable implementation at the reported call site.
The rule does not establish the target platform's precise Java or Android library version.
The rule does not establish whether a concrete implementation follows the Comparable contract when given null.

security_semantics.detector_claim: A contract-violating or suspicious attempt to compare a Comparable value with a null argument was observed at a matched call site.
security_semantics.runtime_claim: Immediately before the matched invocation, the argument value bound to o was null.

source_level: Resolve the invoked compareTo signature and confirm that its AspectJ declaring-type pattern matches java.lang.Comparable+.
Treat a lexical compareTo( match only as a candidate; verify the resolved call rather than selecting another framework's similarly named API.
Do not require a literal null argument in source, because the rule tests the evaluated runtime value.
runtime: Confirm that the invocation was instrumented and that the bound argument o evaluated to null at the before-call join point.
To establish actual outcome, independently capture whether the invocation proceeded and whether it returned or threw an exception.
To establish impact, independently show how the null value arises and whether the resulting behavior is reachable in the relevant deployment.
compatibility: Identify the Java/Android runtime API level used by the application.
Confirm the AspectJ/RV-Monitor weaving or agent configuration covers the relevant call site.
Account for compiler-generated bridge methods, desugaring, proxies, and Kotlin-to-JVM compilation where applicable.

known_false_positive_shapes: A test intentionally invokes compareTo with null to verify the documented NullPointerException behavior.
A program deliberately invokes a nonconforming custom Comparable implementation that accepts null; the rule still reports the null call even if that implementation does not throw.
A report consumer classifies every monitor warning as a security issue even though this rule records an API-contract condition and has no security-impact predicate.
A report is attributed to a broad enclosing method such as handleIntent even though the actual matched invocation is in generated, synthetic, bridge, or nested code associated with that method.
unknowns: The rule file does not disclose the value of __DEFAULT_MESSAGE, so the representative combined message cannot be fully attributed to a literal in the rule.
The rule does not state which concrete compareTo declaration or receiver type produced the representative finding.
The rule alone cannot show whether name.gdr.acastus_photon.MainActivity.handleIntent was executed in production, test, or analysis instrumentation.
The rule does not prove whether the null value was expected, validated, attacker-controlled, or harmful.

The Java SE 6 document cited in the rule phrases null handling as compareTo(null) "should" throw NullPointerException, whereas current Oracle API documentation formally lists NullPointerException for a null argument; the rule itself does not select a target API version.
